\chapter{Goods and Sacks}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مال} (māl)}{مال (māl)}]{\ur{مال} (māl) — goods (for sale); stock}

\label{lesson:UR-C424-mal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a discount, then the Urdu for a sale (at low prices).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مال}}
\textbf{\ur{مال}} — \emph{māl} — \textquotedblleft{}goods (for sale); stock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکان} \ur{میں} \ur{نیا} \ur{مال} \ur{آیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukān meṅ nayā māl āyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
New stock has come into the shop.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مال}} (\emph{māl}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{māl}, \textquotedblleft{}property, wealth\textquotedblright{}; in a shop it is the goods for sale.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukān meṅ nayā māl āyā.} — New stock has come into the shop.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a discount, then the Urdu for a sale (at low prices), then say \emph{māl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{مال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Goods (for sale); stock\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ذخیرہ} (zakhīrā)}{ذخیرہ (zakhīrā)}]{\ur{ذخیرہ} (zakhīrā) — a stockpile; a store (of goods)}

\label{lesson:UR-C424-zakhira}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a sale (at low prices), then the Urdu for goods (for sale).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ذخیرہ}}
\textbf{\ur{ذخیرہ}} — \emph{zakhīrā} — \textquotedblleft{}a stockpile; a store (of goods)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{چینی} \ur{کا} \ur{بڑا} \ur{ذخیرہ} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār ke pās chīnī kā baṛā zakhīrā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper has a big stock of sugar.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ذخیرہ}} (\emph{zakhīrā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dhakhīra}, \textquotedblleft{}a store, provisions\textquotedblright{}; Urdu says its \textbf{\ur{ذ}} as a \emph{z}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zakhīrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukāndār ke pās chīnī kā baṛā zakhīrā hai.} — The shopkeeper has a big stock of sugar.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a sale (at low prices), then the Urdu for goods (for sale), then say \emph{zakhīrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بوری} (borī)}{بوری (borī)}]{\ur{بوری} (borī) — a sack}

\label{lesson:UR-C424-bori}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for goods (for sale), then the Urdu for a stockpile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بوری}}
\textbf{\ur{بوری}} — \emph{borī} — \textquotedblleft{}a sack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مزدور} \ur{نے} \ur{چاول} \ur{کی} \ur{بوری} \ur{اٹھائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mazdūr ne chāval kī borī uṭhāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The labourer lifted the sack of rice.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بوری}} (\emph{borī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousins \emph{borā}, \textquotedblleft{}a gunny bag\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{borī} under \emph{bōra}, \textquotedblleft{}sacking, a sack\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 9320).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیکٹ} (paikaṭ)}{پیکٹ (paikaṭ)}]{\ur{پیکٹ} (paikaṭ) — a packet}

\label{lesson:UR-C424-paikat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a stockpile, then the Urdu for a sack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیکٹ}}
\textbf{\ur{پیکٹ}} — \emph{paikaṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a packet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{بسکٹ} \ur{کا} \ur{ایک} \ur{پیکٹ} \ur{خریدا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne biskuṭ kā ek paikaṭ kharīdā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I bought a packet of biscuits.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پیکٹ}} (\emph{paikaṭ}) is borrowed from English \emph{packet}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لپیٹنا} (lapeṭnā)}{لپیٹنا (lapeṭnā)}]{\ur{لپیٹنا} (lapeṭnā) — to wrap}

\label{lesson:UR-C424-lapetna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a sack, then the Urdu for a packet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لپیٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{لپیٹنا}} — \emph{lapeṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to wrap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{نے} \ur{کتاب} \ur{کاغذ} \ur{میں} \ur{لپیٹی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār ne kitāb kāghaz meṅ lapeṭī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper wrapped the book in paper.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{تحفہ} \ur{لپیٹا}, \emph{us ne tohfā lapeṭā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لپیٹنا}} (\emph{lapeṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lapeṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to wrap, to fold\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{lappēṭṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}wrap\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10942).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lapeṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukāndār ne kitāb kāghaz meṅ lapeṭī.} — The shopkeeper wrapped the book in paper.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a sack, then the Urdu for a packet, then say \emph{lapeṭnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
